title: The Jurors Apologized
sentences: Five years later, twelve jurors signed an apology.
In January 1697, Massachusetts set aside a day of fasting over the tragedy.
That day, Judge Samuel Sewall stood in his Boston church while his confession of guilt was read aloud.
Twelve trial jurors signed a statement saying they had been sadly deluded and mistaken.
They asked forgiveness from the people they had wronged.
In 1706, accuser Ann Putnam apologized in church too.
caption:
Five years after Salem, twelve jurors admitted they were wrong.
